references.raw: Trepanowski et al., 2017, JAMA Internal Medicine. "Effect of Alternate-Day Fasting on Weight Loss, Weight Maintenance, and Cardioprotection Among Metabolically Healthy Obese Adults." At 12 months, alternate-day fasting and daily calorie restriction produced similar weight loss, and the fasting group had a higher dropout rate.
references.title: Effect of Alternate-Day Fasting on Weight Loss, Weight Maintenance, and Cardioprotection Among Metabolically Healthy Obese Adults

references.raw: Liu et al., 2022, New England Journal of Medicine. "Calorie Restriction with or without Time-Restricted Eating in Weight Loss." Adding an 8-hour eating window to calorie restriction gave no additional weight loss at 12 months.
references.title: Calorie Restriction with or without Time-Restricted Eating in Weight Loss

references.raw: Lowe et al., 2020, JAMA Internal Medicine. "Effects of Time-Restricted Eating on Weight Loss and Other Metabolic Parameters in Women and Men With Overweight and Obesity" (the TREAT trial). Time-restricted eating did not produce significantly more weight loss than a control group eating three meals a day.
references.title: Effects of Time-Restricted Eating on Weight Loss and Other Metabolic Parameters in Women and Men With Overweight and Obesity

references.raw: Sundfør et al., 2018, Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases. A trial of continuous versus intermittent (5:2-style) energy restriction. I recall similar outcomes, but I'm less certain of the exact title and details.
Cioffi et al., 2018, Journal of Translational Medicine. A meta-analysis of intermittent versus continuous energy restriction. Weight loss and cardiometabolic outcomes were broadly similar.

Patikorn et al., 2021, JAMA Network Open. "Intermittent Fasting and Obesity-Related Health Outcomes: An Umbrella Review of Meta-analyses of Randomized Clinical Trials." Found modest benefits versus no intervention, with little difference versus continuous restriction.
references.title: Intermittent Fasting and Obesity-Related Health Outcomes: An Umbrella Review of Meta-analyses of Randomized Clinical Trials
